summary: Keep MinerPass JSON schema v1 independent of operation rules v2
details: Mint JSON uses integer v=1 while zero-balance opening, source checks, ownership history and cross-address inheritance continue to execute state-machine v2. The payload version cannot select the retired permissive state machine.

Withdraw the development schema v2 accepted by testnet-v1 r1-r4 without adding a payload alias or a legacy executor. Update wallet drafts, post-mint verification, RPC fixtures and protocol documentation to distinguish schema from operation rules.

Regenerate scoped registries, active-version identities, Rust/Go golden vectors and the resettable testnet-v1 bundle. Preserve chain/network IDs, Bitcoin origin, genesis allocation and genesis block hash; update the genesis configuration digest and runtime data identities.
operator_actions: Upgrade all testnet-v1 miners, followers and indexers together. The new release derives a new indexer path, but the USDB-chain directory name is unchanged: explicitly provision an empty chain data directory for the development reset. Do not import prior indexer or USDB-chain state; reuse Bitcoin and balance-history data only under the existing compatibility checks.

After selecting the updated release, mint with integer v=1 and verify the intended pass, source and recipient before funding a new cold address. JSON v=2 from the withdrawn development configuration is no longer accepted.
